title.narrative: THE FISCAL GOVERNANCE AND INSTITUTIONS PROJECT

description.narrative: The development objective of Fiscal Governance and Institutions Project for Nigeria is to improve the credibility of public finance and national statistics. The project consists of the following four components. 1) The first component, Strengthening revenue management, aims at enhancing oversight of revenues accruing to the Federation account; and strengthening revenue analysis and forecasting to help retrieve unremitted revenues and improve revenue outturn. It has the following two subcomponents: (i) Strengthening of the oversight of Federation revenue through external and internal auditing; and (ii) Strengthening revenue analysis and forecasting. 2) The second component, Strengthening controls, transparency and accountability in the use of public funds, aims at operationalizing the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS) for payment controls, cash management and budget execution Monitoring and Evaluation (M and E), strengthening Public Investment Management (PIM) and improving transparency and efficiency in the use of public funds through enhanced procurement and the quality of budget information. It has the following three subcomponents: (i) Operationalization of the GIFMIS for budget management and reporting; (ii) Strengthening PIM; and (iii) Improving transparency and efficiency in procurement, and the quality of budget information. 3) The third component, Strengthening economic and fiscal statistics, aims at generating and validating economic statistics and reconciling them with fiscal data. It has the following two subcomponents: (i) Improvement of economic statistics; and (ii) Reconciliation, validation, archiving, and dissemination of official statistics. 4) The fourth component, Implementation support, aims to finance the activities and functioning of the implementation framework.
To improve the credibility of public finance and national statistics.

condition.narrative: The Recipient shall furnish to the Association each Project Report not later than one month after the end of each calendarsemester, covering the calendar semester (Schedule 2, Section II.A of the Financing Agreement).

The Recipient shall within each of the Implementing Agencies, with the exception of the FMOF, establish, no later than two (2)months after the Effective Date and thereafter maintain, throughout the implementation of the Project, a Project ImplementationUnit with functions, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association and as elaborated in the POM (Schedule 2, SectionI.A.2 of the Financing Agreement).

The Recipient shall within the CAC, establish no later than two (2) months after countersignature of this Amendment and thereaftermaintain, throughout the implementation of the Project, a Project Implementation Unit with functions, composition and resourcessatisfactory to the Association and as elaborated in the POM.

The Recipient shall, no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, appoint an external auditor, under terms of referenceacceptable to the Association, to audit the Office of the Auditor General of the Federation (Schedule 2, Section I.E of theFinancing Agreement).

The Recipient shall, within the FMoF, establish, no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date and thereafter maintain,throughout the implementation of the Project, a Project coordination unit (PCU) with functions, resources and staffing in adequatenumber satisfactory to the Association and as elaborated in the POM (Schedule 2, Section I.A.1 of the Financing Agreement).

The Recipient, through FoOF, shall no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by theAssociation, appoint and thereafter maintain, at all times during the implementation of the Project, an independent verification agent with qualifications and experience and under terms of reference acceptable to the Association (“Verification Agent”), to verify the data and other evidence supporting the achievement of one or more DLIs as set forth in the table in Schedule4 and recommend corresponding payments to be made, as applicable, under Category 2 (Schedule 2, Section I.C.1 of the FinancingAgreement).

title.narrative: Publication of reconcilied fiscal and economic datasets
Enhanced functionality of the financial management information systems (PBC /DLI 3)

baseline.value: GIFMIS payment controls and cash management modules not operational. Monthly Treasury Statements, Daily Payment Reports covering payments of at least 10 Million Naira, Monthly Budget Performance Reports generated by GIFMIS by MDAs, Monthly Fiscal Accounts and Unaudited quarterly financial statements by MDA and unaudited consolidated quarterly financial statements and annual audited financial statements Government-Owned Enterprises (GoEs) are not published on the Open Treasury Portal. Payments to vendors under FGN capital budget are processed by MDAs and FGOEs.

target.value: A Circular introducing centralized disbursement processes is approved and issued by HMoF ; OAGF makes payments under FGN budget capital expenditures directly to vendors based on warrants issued by HMoF, in line with the government bottom-up cash planning policy

actual.value: The FMF has issued a policy to introduce the a centralized disbursement processes. Under the revised policy, the OAGF makes payments for capital expenditures directly to vendors based on warrants issued by HMoF, in line with the government bottom-up cash planning policy.

baseline.value: No agriculture and business census. Labor Force Surveys, Living Standards and Job Creation Surveys are not conducted. There is no administrative statistics system and no SDG tracking system. There is no strategy for statistical development. Methods of food price data collection using artificial intelligence (AI) are not used. Methodology for the state GDP production is not consistent with the national GDP.

target.value: The first and second quarters of job creation survey completed ; annual business establishment survey completed and published on NBS web-site ; SDGs tracking completion report is available and published on NBS microdata library ; the first phase of Administrative Statistics System, covering not less than six MDAs, is completed; methodology for the state GDP production consistent with national GDP, is prepared and published at NBS microdata library; alternative methods of food price data collection using artificial intelligence (AI) and crowdsourcing are used by NBS

actual.value: NBS has also published the Business Sample Census and 1st round of Labor Force Survey. Field work of listing of Agriculture Census has been completed and disbursed against. Agriculture Sample Census completed and disbursed. 2nd round Labor Force Survey are completed, verified and disbursed. The first half of field work for the Nigeria Living Standards Survey, completed, verified and disbursed. The second half of the field work for the Nigeria Living Standards Survey completed and under verification. 3rd and 4th rounds of Labor Force Survey have been completed and under verification. National Strategy on Development of Statistics (NSDS) for 2024-2028 approved by NBS board (NBS). The implementation continues with a delay. NBS has prepared a draft NSDS, organized a validation workshop in April and the Strategy has been approved..

title.narrative: Regular internal and external audit reports completed (PBC /DLI 1)

baseline.value: No external revenue audits; occasional internal audits

target.value: Revenue assurance audit of Main Income Generating Agencies (including FIRS and NCS) for 2020 and 2021 completed

actual.value: The IVA report concluded that IRs 1.3, 1.5 and 1.6 which for fiscal years 2019/2020/2021 by OAuGF have not been achieved due to limited evidence that the Revenue Assurance audits were conducted in accordance with International Standards for Supreme Audit Institutions. IVA report noted that the audit reports submitted to the National Assembly for the FIRS and the NCS were management letters addressed to the auditees which are not acceptable as audit reports. The IVA Verification Report also concluded that PBCs 1.4 and 1.7 on completing IT audit reports for fiscal years 2019 and 2021 by the OAuGF was not achieved because the reports were not submitted for verification at all, despite several follow-ups on same.

baseline.value: Occasional and inadequate revenue analysis; weak revenue models. Foreign Currency Denominated inflows from FGOEs are not accounted in FGN budget. Internal revenue from FGOEs are remitted to CRF with delays.

target.value: Revenues of all FGOEs are split and automatically remitted to CRF/TSA-Sub Recurrent Account based on the relevant Finance Circular ; a new TSA sub-account is established for Foreign Currency Denominated inflows covering at least 55 FGOEs; Revenue Assurance Billing and Collections digital solution is implemented

actual.value: Currently, the revenues of FGOEs are split at the FGOEs and automatically remitted to CRF/TSA-Sub Recurrent Account based on the relevant Finance Circular. A new TSA sub-account is established for Foreign Currency Denominated inflows covering at least 55 FGOEs; Revenue Assurance Billing and Collections digital solution has been designed but yet to be rolled out.

title.narrative: Strengthened monitoring and evaluation of public investment projects (PBC /DLI 4)

baseline.value: PIM guideline as an annex to the budget circular is not in place

target.value: Compliance rate with PIM guidelines in at least two MDAs with largescale capital budgets; deployment of a National Budget Portal to publish Government of Nigeriaâ€™s (FGN and at least 20 States) approved capital projects (including supplementary budgets, if any); deployment of GIFMIS capital/project module in 10 MDAs

actual.value: Revised PIM guidelines were annexed to the 2023 Budget Circular. Compliance rate with PIM guidelines in at least two MDAs with largescale capital budgets is under verification. Budget Portal software has been developed and undergoing data quality assurance. Deployment of GIFMIS capital/project module in 10 MDAs has been verified as achieved. Capital project tracking system for 10 MDAs is not feasible to implement before relevant policy is introduced. BOF has proposed including this requirement in the Draft Budget Implementation Guideline.

title.narrative: Enhanced effectiveness and transparency of FGN asset management (PBC/DLI 7)

baseline.value: National Asset Registry (NAR) demo is developed however it does not contain information on historical financials and boards composition for MOFI portfolio companies (PCs). NAR is not publicly available; a Report on SOEs - MOFI PCs - is not available

target.value: NAR registry showing MOFI kickoff portfolio corporate assets, historical financial information for at least 3 years (for at least 50% of PCs), shareholding & corporate governance practices is available to the public through the FMoF and the MOFI websites; a Portfolio report providing key information on the financial health of the MOFI PCs for the year 2023 is available to the public through the FMoF and the MOFI websites

actual.value: The template for the publication of AFS in MOFI's website under preparation. The discussion corporate governance scorecard is ongoing.

baseline.value: SOE Portfolio management policy is not available; audited financial statements are not consistently published by SOEs including MOFI PCs; Nigeria Code of Corporate Governance was approved in 2018, but there is no Scorecard to measure the extent of compliance with the policies by MOFI kick off PCs

target.value: MOFI portfolio management policy that details policies and procedures for managing SOEs - MOFI PCs is developed and approved by the Federal Executive Council; audited financial statements for FY2023 are published by at least 50% of the MOFI kick off PCs at MOFI website; A Corporate Governance Scorecard for SOEs - MOFI PCs - is developed, approved by MOFI Board and implemented by at least 50% of MOFI kick off PCs. The Scorecard is published at FMoF and MOFI websites

actual.value: MOFI has completed the procurement process for the engagement of the consultant to prepare the policies and procedures for managing SOE. MOFI plan to complete the process by end of CY 2024. The discussion for the development of corporate governance scorecard for Nigeria is ongoing in close collaboration with key stakeholders. MOFI has planned for the Corporate Governance Forum in Q1 of 2025.
